title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: Why does chilled candour matter more in an investigation than in most settings? `[V]`
options: Because witnesses have a right to speak freely under employment law
Because the employer's own defence depends on the investigation having been prompt and effective, so a tool that reduces what witnesses will say attacks the thing you are relying on
Because reluctant witnesses produce inadmissible evidence
Because chilled witnesses are more likely to bring their own claims
questions.explanation: An investigation that reached no conclusion because two witnesses declined is not a neutral outcome — it is a weaker position for the employer and a worse one for the complainant.

questions.prompt: Which mitigation does the module say costs the least and protects the most?
options: Obtaining written consent from every participant in advance
Never transcribing the first contact, where chilling costs most and the record is worth least
Deleting transcripts once the summary is written
Using a human transcriber rather than an automated one
questions.explanation: The initial intake conversation is where somebody decides whether to proceed at all. Take notes. C is worse than useless once a hold may apply.

questions.prompt: What is the exposure created by transcription that people most often miss?
options: That transcripts can be inaccurate
That transcripts must be disclosed to the employee
That it creates a comprehensive timestamped record that would not otherwise have existed — every clumsy question, aside, and piece of preamble, now producible in full
That transcripts are harder to redact than notes
questions.explanation: Your notes were always a selective reconstruction. A transcript is everything, including the five minutes about a third party who is not involved in this matter.

options: Machine transcripts should be produced by a human transcriber for verification
Keep contemporaneous notes separately, review the transcript against them for attribution and unmarked inaudibility before filing, and never file an unreviewed transcript
Transcripts should only be used for interviews conducted remotely
Notes should be destroyed once a transcript exists
questions.explanation: And corrections are visible and dated rather than silent — a silently edited transcript is worse than either the original or your notes.

questions.prompt: In an all-party consent jurisdiction, what makes recording lawful? `[V]`
options: A notice in the employee handbook
The visible presence of a notetaker bot in the meeting
Every participant's agreement — and the controlling question is where the participants are, not where you are
The employer's legitimate business interest in accurate records
questions.explanation: "The bot joined the call" is not consent, and a single witness in an all-party state can change what is lawful for that interview.

questions.prompt: What does the February 2026 biometric class action theory make the exposure? `[V]`
options: The content of the transcript
Who was given access to the recording
The transcription feature itself capturing voice biometric data without proper consent — independent of what the transcript says or whether anyone used it
The retention period applied to the recording
questions.explanation: Which means a recording you never used, in a matter that went nowhere, is still within the theory. Litigation is active; this is on the module's counsel list.

questions.prompt: Why is unequal transcription accuracy a due-process problem as well as a discrimination one? `[V]`
options: Because inaccurate transcripts are inadmissible

Because a materially worse transcript for a non-native-speaking respondent means their account reaches the decision-maker less accurately than their accuser's — and the transcript is the evidence of that
Because it violates data-accuracy obligations
Because it requires disclosure to the affected participant
questions.explanation: Which is why quality has to be checked **by speaker** rather than in aggregate — an overall accuracy figure hides exactly the pattern that matters. And where it is poorer, the answer is your notes and a human review, not a better prompt.

questions.prompt: What does Weingarten constrain about recording? `[V]`
options: It prohibits recording without the representative's consent
It requires the employee's written consent before recording

Nothing — the decision does not forbid an employer from recording an investigatory interview; the real constraints are consent law, candour, your collective agreement, and possibly the duty to bargain
It permits recording only where discipline is not contemplated
questions.explanation: A common and useful thing to get right. Weingarten governs the right to representation on request in an investigatory interview that could lead to discipline — not the recording. And a representative in the room means your record is no longer the only record.
